verdict.rationale: Cline's CLI documents cron-scheduled agents through a hub. These agents persist across process restarts and run independently of any terminal session. Headless runs in GitHub Actions or GitLab pipelines plus auto-approve allow unattended execution, such as "run tests and fix failures". The scheduling docs only name recurring tasks like daily summaries and code reviews, not autonomous maintenance and fixing. Event triggers depend on external CI pipelines rather than a native trigger system. missing for 10: native event/webhook trigger configuration within Cline, documented scheduled maintenance/fix workflows (beyond summaries and reviews), independent or hands-on corroboration of scheduled autonomous operation.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can set up always-on agents that run on schedules or triggers to maintain and fix my software autonomously

citations.quote: Scheduled agents persist across process restarts and run independently of any terminal session.
Run agents on cron schedules for recurring automations like daily summaries and code reviews.
Run it headlessly inside GitHub Actions, GitLab, or any pipeline.
cline --auto-approve true "run tests and fix failures"
Cline auto-approves everything: file changes, terminal commands, browser actions, MCP tools, and mode transitions.
